title: When AI Performance Is Not Enough: Statistical Guardrails for Clinical Development
abstract: arXiv:2611.28497v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are reshaping the operational and inferential landscape of clinical development, yet their adoption frequently outpaces the statistical scrutiny these methods demand. This commentary offers first-principles perspectives across four application domains: anomaly detection in clinical trial data, real-time monitoring and adaptive trial designs, biomarker-based enrichment, and virtual and digital twins. For each domain, we articulate the underlying inferential problem, the contribution of AI and ML relative to established statistical methods, and the risks that statisticians, data scientists, and clinical developers must actively manage. Across these domains, a unifying theme emerges: AI and ML methods may succeed locally while failing to satisfy the broader statistical assumptions required for valid clinical and regulatory decisions. translated_title: 当AI性能不足够时：临床开发中的统计防护栏
translated_abstract: 人工智能（AI）和机器学习（ML）正在重塑临床开发的运营和推断格局，然而它们的应用速度往往超过了这些方法所需的统计审查。本文从第一性原理的视角审视了四个应用领域：临床试验数据中的异常检测、实时监测与适应性试验设计、基于生物标志物的富集，以及虚拟和数字孪生。针对每个领域，我们阐明了其背后的推断问题、AI和ML相对于既有统计方法的贡献，以及统计学家、数据科学家和临床开发人员必须主动管理的风险。贯穿这些领域的一个统一主题是：AI和ML方法可能在局部取得成功，却无法满足有效的临床和监管决策所需的更广泛的统计假设。这些风险包括假阳性信号、受损的（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文指出AI和ML方法虽然在临床试验的异常检测、适应性设计、生物标志物富集和数字孪生等领域可能局部表现出色，但往往无法满足有效临床与监管决策所需的统计假设，因此必须建立统计防护栏来管控假阳性信号等风险。
en_tdlr: This commentary argues that AI and ML methods may succeed locally in clinical development—across anomaly detection, adaptive trial designs, biomarker enrichment, and digital twins—while failing to satisfy broader statistical assumptions required for valid clinical and regulatory decisions, necessitating statistical guardrails.
